tldr: Speculative decoding — drafting candidate tokens ahead of the target model to cut serving latency — is a known lever for LLM inference cost. NVIDIA's June 23 developer post introduced DFlash, a speculator built on the target model's own KV projections, claiming up to 15x throughput gains on Blackwell GPUs.
whats_new: Modal named DFlash as the technique behind its own state-of-the-art inference-latency results, working with Z Lab and SGLang to release open-source pre-trained speculator models — including one for Qwen that improves over multi-token prediction by more than 50%.
why_it_matters: If you're running inference on Blackwell GPUs with SGLang, this is now an off-the-shelf latency lever: Modal reports that Blackwell plus SGLang plus a low-overhead regional deployment can match or beat proprietary inference providers without custom infra.

status.detail: Modal confirms the same DFlash technique in its own latency benchmarks and ships open-source pre-trained speculator models built with Z Lab and SGLang.

beats.headline: NVIDIA introduces DFlash, claiming up to 15x inference gains on Blackwell
beats.summary: DFlash generates draft tokens in parallel using the target model's own KV projections, invented by Jian Chen and collaborators at Z Lab.

beats.headline: Modal ships open-source DFlash speculator models with Z Lab and SGLang
beats.summary: Modal reports DFlash as its best-performing speculative-decoding technique, with a Qwen speculator improving over multi-token prediction by 50%+.

open_questions: Does DFlash's speedup hold on non-Blackwell GPUs, or is it Blackwell-specific?
Will inference frameworks beyond SGLang add native DFlash speculator support?
take_for_builders: Running inference on Blackwell with SGLang? Evaluate the open-source DFlash speculator models before building custom speculative decoding — Modal reports it matching proprietary inference-provider latency without proprietary infra.
